answer: To resist Sybil swarms, nodes verify each identity through cryptographic attestation chains compressed into zero-knowledge proofs. Minting an agent identity requires staking capital that scales exponentially (O(2^n)) per additional instance linked to an origin cluster. Each verified credential acts like a permanent relic anchored to a historical voyage of valid execution, turning the attacker’s cost into an insurmountable tide that forces exponential capital exhaustion.
